description: Agua de Jamaica, a vibrant and refreshing hibiscus tea, is a staple in Mexican households. Its tart, floral notes and beautiful ruby color make it a perfect beverage for any meal or a hot day. This traditional agua fresca is simple to prepare and offers a delightful taste of Mexico.

instructions.title: Prepare the Hibiscus Concentrate
instructions.text: In a large saucepan, combine 4 cups of water and the dried hibiscus flowers. Bring the water to a rolling boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer gently for 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Steep and Cool
instructions.text: After simmering, remove the saucepan from the heat. Let the hibiscus flowers steep in the hot water for another 15-20 minutes. This allows the flowers to fully release their vibrant color and tart flavor. The liquid should become a deep, rich red.

instructions.title: Strain the Concentrate
instructions.text: Place a fine-mesh sieve over a large pitcher or heatproof bowl. Carefully pour the hibiscus mixture through the sieve, pressing gently on the rehydrated flowers with the back of a spoon to extract all the liquid. Discard the spent hibiscus flowers.

instructions.title: Sweeten the Concentrate
instructions.text: Add 1/2 cup of granulated sugar to the strained hibiscus concentrate. Stir well until the sugar is completely dissolved. Taste the concentrate and add more sugar, up to 1 cup total, if you prefer a sweeter drink. Remember it will be diluted later.

instructions.title: Dilute and Adjust Flavor
instructions.text: Pour the remaining 4 cups of cold water into the sweetened hibiscus concentrate. Stir thoroughly to combine. At this point, you can add the juice of one lime if desired, which brightens the flavor beautifully. Taste and adjust sweetness or tartness as needed.

instructions.title: Chill and Serve
instructions.text: Refrigerate the Agua de Jamaica for at least 1 hour, or until thoroughly chilled. Serve over plenty of ice in tall glasses. Garnish with a slice of lime or a fresh mint sprig if you like. Enjoy this refreshing Mexican beverage!

tips: For a deeper color and flavor, you can lightly toast the dried hibiscus flowers in a dry pan for a minute before adding water.
Adjust the amount of sugar to your liking; some prefer it very tart, while others enjoy it sweeter. You can also use honey or agave nectar as natural sweeteners.
Agua de Jamaica is best served very cold over ice. It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For a festive touch, add fresh fruit like berries or orange slices to the pitcher.
